record.paper_title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics
record.original_question: Find natural families of one-variable elliptic holomorphic germs of the form f_{λ,a}(z)=λz+z^2 g_a(z), parametrized by a in some parameter space M, for which holomorphic linearizability is equivalent exactly to the Brjuno condition on the multiplier λ. In particular, is every elliptic polynomial, or even every elliptic cubic polynomial, holomorphically linearizable if and only if its multiplier is a Brjuno number?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C},0)$ denote the set of holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$. A germ is called elliptic if it has the form
$$f(z)=\lambda z+z^2 g(z),$$
where $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\theta}$ with $\theta\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ and $g$ is holomorphic at $0$. Such an $f$ is said to be holomorphically linearizable if there exists a local biholomorphism $\varphi:(\mathbb{C},0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ such that $\varphi^{-1}\circ f\circ \varphi(z)=\lambda z$ in some neighborhood of $0$.

An irrational number $\theta$ with continued fraction convergents $p_n/q_n$ is called a Brjuno number if
$$\sum_{n\geq 0}\frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n}<\infty,$$
and a multiplier $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\theta}$ is called Brjuno when $\theta$ is Brjuno.

Problem. Identify natural families
$$\{f_{\lambda,a}(z)=\lambda z+z^2 g_a(z)\}_{a\in M}\subset\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C},0)$$
of elliptic germs, parametrized by $a$ in some space $M$, with the property that $f_{\lambda,a}$ is holomorphically linearizable if and only if $\lambda$ is a Brjuno number. In particular, decide the following:

(a) Is every elliptic polynomial $f(z)=\lambda z+a_2 z^2+\cdots+a_d z^d$ holomorphically linearizable at $0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a Brjuno number?

(b) Is every elliptic cubic polynomial $f(z)=\lambda z+a_2 z^2+a_3 z^3$ holomorphically linearizable at $0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a Brjuno number?
artifact.status_search_result: The Brjuno condition is known to be necessary and sufficient for the quadratic family (Yoccoz). For higher-degree polynomials, including cubics, the necessity of the Brjuno condition for linearizability remains open; this is connected to a long-standing conjecture of Douady that for any rational map of degree at least 2, an irrationally indifferent periodic point with non-Brjuno rotation number is not linearizable. No definitive resolution for cubics or general polynomials appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Siegel disks (Scholarpedia draft, X. Buff)
status_evidence.snippet: It remains open whether there exist cubic polynomials with non-Brjuno linearizable fixed points; Douady conjectured the Brjuno condition is necessary for all rational maps of degree ≥ 2.
status_evidence.claim: The cubic polynomial case of necessity of the Brjuno condition is still open.

status_evidence.title: Geyer, Siegel Discs, Herman Rings and the Arnold Family
status_evidence.snippet: Following Yoccoz's proof, necessity of the Brjuno condition has been established for various families, but not in general beyond quadratics.
status_evidence.claim: Necessity is known for quadratics (Yoccoz) but not generally.
